Photograph: Ahn young-joon/AP South Korea South Korea calls for apology from North Korea after mine injures three soldiers Blast during search operation near border fuels political tensions amid attempts to revive diplomatic channels Raphael Rashid in Seoul Wed 30 Sep 2026 03.53 EDT Last modified on Wed 30 Sep 2026 04.34 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google South Korea has demanded an apology from North Korea over a landmine blast that injured three soldiers, saying they were hurt by North Korean mines on the southern side of the border. Kang Hyun-woo, the director of operations at South Korea’s joint chiefs of staff, demanded an apology and “responsible measures” from Pyongyang over the blast, which occurred on 21 September during a search operation south of the border. He also called for an immediate halt to North Korea’s mine-laying and border fortification, which he said violated the armistice and the spirit of inter-Korean agreements. North Korea would bear “all responsibility” for any future developments, he said. Why is South Korea so angry with Ukraine over two North Korean prisoners of war? Read more The incident echoes a 2015 mine blast in the demilitarised zone between the countries that seriously injured two South Korean soldiers and prompted Seoul to resume propaganda broadcasts over loudspeakers. North Korea responded to the move with artillery fire across the border before expressing regret during high-level talks . The US-led UN command (UNC), which oversees the 1953 armistice that halted but did not end the Korean war, said on Wednesday that a joint investigation with South Korea’s military had identified a live North Korean anti-personnel mine on the southern side of the military demarcation line (MDL), the de facto border. The UNC said an armistice violation had occurred and that it was addressing the issue through “established armistice mechanisms”. The explosions occurred about 10 metres south of the MDL on the western front, as troops searched an area where North Korea was suspected of laying mines. Two blasts went off about a minute apart, seriously injuring a battalion commander, whose foot was reportedly severed at the ankle, and an engineer. A third officer was present and has minor injuries from the explosion. On Monday, South Korea’s military said interim findings showed the blasts were “highly likely” to have been caused by North Korean mines North Korea has denied involvement. In a statement carried by state media on Wednesday, Kim Yo-jong, the sister of leader Kim Jong-un , called the incident “an obvious self-staged farce”. “Our soldiers have never once crossed the border,” she said, warning that if South Korean troops fired directly at North Korean soldiers, border units would carry out “immediate and merciless retaliation”. View image in fullscreen Kim Yo-jong, seen here in 2022, has denied any North Korean involvement in the incident. Photograph: 朝鮮通信社/AP Chris Green, a senior consultant at the International Crisis Group, said the investigation findings would not settle the matter politically because the North would always have “guaranteed plausible deniability”. There are no working communication channels between the two Koreas. Pyongyang severed ties in 2024, declared South Korea a hostile state and has since laid mines and built fortifications along the border. “Accidental escalation on the Korean peninsula is always just a few steps away and it’s fewer steps now than it was in 2015,” Green said. The blast presents a challenge for South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung , who has sought to revive diplomacy with Pyongyang. Last week, he told the UN general assembly that Seoul would be a “pacemaker” for peace, and urged Washington to ease sanctions in exchange for a freeze on North Korea’s weapons programmes. The incident has also fuelled political tensions at home. Opposition politicians questioned whether the investigation had been delayed to avoid overshadowing Lee’s UN speech, a suggestion the presidential office denied. The conservative People Power party has also called for the return of the propaganda loudspeakers, which were switched off and dismantled under Lee last year. The mine blast adds to other diplomatic difficulties facing Lee. On Monday, Seoul demanded an apology from Ukraine after its president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, disclosed the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea. Seoul said the two sides had agreed to keep the transfer secret, citing the men’s safety and diplomatic and security considerations. Some critics said the secrecy was about not upsetting Pyongyang. https://www.breitbart.com/europe/2026/11.text: Polish President Karol Nawrocki has accused Prime Minister Donald Tusk of plunging the nation into a “serious constitutional crisis” and committing “crimes against the Constitution” after a dramatic spat over the composition of the nation’s top court over the weekend. The long-simmering battle between Tusk’s left-liberal faction and the conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party broke out into literal conflict in the early hours of Saturday morning, as riot police were deployed to the Constitutional Tribunal, as its chief judge was locked out of the building, and as an ally of the prime minister, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, having declared herself as the new leader and said she would be dismissing the PiS-aligned president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and vice president Bartłomiej Sochański of the top court. In a sensational move, President Nawrocki cut short a trip to Senegal and immediately returned to Warsaw, where he physically forced his way into the Tribunal building in a bid to stop what he and his allies have claimed was an attempted “coup” over the judiciary by the Tusk-led government, which claims that the right to appoint judges lies solely with the Sejm parliament, while rejecting President Nawrocki’s claim that his office has final approval over any appointments. The dispute continued into the week, with Korwin-Piotrowska continuing to claim control of the tribunal, despite PiS allies boycotting meetings, resulting in a farcical situation in which the liberal judges claim that 8 of 15 justices now represent a two-thirds quorum. Meanwhile, Święczkowski continues to claim that he is the court’s legitimate head and rejects Korwin-Piotrowska’s right to suspend him. At a meeting of the National Security Council on Tuesday, President Nawrocki accused Tusk of “deciding to take over an independent institution of the Polish state by force on the eve of the holidays” and of having “exploited” police officers to “further a political agenda”. “The rule of law cannot be restored by methods that themselves flagrantly violate the law… Full responsibility for this entire situation, for every police officer at the Tribunal, for all illegal actions such as the suspension of judges, illegal orders, and entering the Tribunal from the Prime Minister’s office, rests with one man, a man who is present in this room, a man I smile at, even though I do not understand, do not accept, and am speaking out against, namely Prime Minister Donald Tusk, ” he said according to the Super Express newspaper. Nawrocki accused the PM of “a crime against the Constitution of the Republic of Poland” for seeking to subvert what he claims is his role as a check and balance by backing appointments to the court solely through parliament, without the president swearing them in. “This is not how democrats operate, Mr Prime Minister… I will not ignore this; I will use all the prerogatives available to me, as well as the legitimacy and mandate given to me by society, to stop this attempt to overturn the constitutional order of the Republic of Poland,” he vowed. Nawrocki, elected president last year, has continued his predecessor Andrzej Duda’s efforts to stymie the liberal Tusk agenda, using his veto power on legislation a record 41 times this year. However, Duda has questioned his move to selectively block judicial appointments by refusing to swear them in, expressing his interpretation that the process was meant to be merely ceremonial rather than a constitutional check and balance. While some, including firebrand Polish Member of the European Parliament Dominik Tarczyński, have claimed that the battle over the Tribunal is, in reality, about attempts to block the Tusk government from diminishing Polish sovereignty and ceding ground to Brussels by, for example, abandoning the złoty currency in favour of the Euro. Yet, with elections looming next year, others have suggested that Tusk is simply trying to replicate the previous PiS strategy and shackle any future right-wing government by packing the court before they come to power. Indeed, although Tusk’s pro-EU Civic Coalition party currently stands as the most popular single party in the country, recent polling has suggested that his left-liberal coalition government is set to lose power at the 2027 election. A survey conducted last week — before the dramatic events outside the Constitutional Tribunal — found that Tusk’s party currently stands at 33.44 per cent, compared to 22.35 per cent for the conservative PiS party. However, with the addition of the nationalist Confederation Liberty and Independence and the Confederation of the Polish Crown parties, as well as former PiS PM Mateusz Morawiecki’s Development Plus party, the right-wing stands at a collective 47.62 per cent and is likely to win enough seats to control the Sejm. https://bnn-news.com/world/in-poland-the.text: Polish president Karol Nawrocki. · Photo: Gatis Rozenfelds/Valsts kanceleja/Flickr Advertisements On the 3rd of November, the political crisis in Poland worsened even more - nationalist President Karol Nawrocki expressed sharp criticism of the pro-European Prime Minister Donald Tusk, writes Politico. In the course of a harsh exchange of opinions, Nawrocki accused Tusk of using the court to seize power, while the prime minister responded by stating that his actions are necessary to preserve the rule of law in the sixth largest economy of the European Union. Controversies about the justice system go back nearly ten years, and at their center is the politicized appointment of judges of higher court instances by the right-wing party Law and Justice (PiS), which was in power until 2023. Tusk's government and the European Commission have insisted that the court should be reorganized in order to comply with EU norms, and on the 30th of October, the powers of the President of the Constitutional Tribunal and his deputy were suspended. The eight judges elected by Tusk's parliament met on the 3rd of November and announced that their number was sufficient to resume work. Meanwhile, Nawrocki took the opportunity to attack the prime minister during the opening of the meeting of the State Security Council, which was also attended by Tusk and other political leaders. Tusk did not have a chance to respond while the opening was being filmed. Referring to the clashes at the Constitutional Tribunal on the 30th of October, Nawrocki said that all responsibility for any police officer near the court building, for all illegal actions, including the suspension of judges and the issuing of illegal orders, rests on the shoulders of one person - Tusk. The President added that he expects Tusk to curb his government's ambitions and stop the illegal actions against the representatives of the Constitutional Court. Advertisements Tusk has previously accused Nawrocki of aggravating the conflict and called for an end to standing against the judges elected by the parliament. He said the president has an opportunity, which he hopes he will take advantage of: to stop attacking legally elected judges and let them do their jobs. The Polish prime minister also accused Moscow of taking advantage of Poland's political unrest and called on politicians not to become useful idiots while the dispute over the court escalated. The tussle over the Constitutional Tribunal widens Poland's political divide ahead of parliamentary elections scheduled for 2027, fueling the earlier unification of various right-wing nationalist parties against Tusk. Meanwhile, for the prime minister, the crisis can serve as a way to unify the voter base before the elections. Eight judges elected by the current parliament organized a meeting on the afternoon of the 3rd of November under the leadership of Anna Korwin-Piotrowska. Korvina-Piotrowska took over the leadership of the Constitutional Tribunal on the 30th of October. Neither Nawrocki nor the right-wing political forces recognize her authority. Also, Nawrocki refused to accept the oath of five elected judges. Instead, the judges handed over the oath of office to parliament, which Nawrocki believes is null and void.
